First, we rewrite the expression using the definitions of $\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta $ and $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta $:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{3\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } & =\frac{\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }-\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{3(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta })\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we multiply the numerator and the denominator by $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \cdot (\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }-\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )}{3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \cdot (\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta })\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{3(\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \cdot {sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta })} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{1}{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }}-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{3(\frac{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\cdot {sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }})} \\  & =\frac{1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{3{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use $1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta ={sin}^{2}⁡\theta $ to simplify the expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{3{sin}^{2}⁡\theta } & =\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{3{sin}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\cancel{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }}{3\cancel{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that:

$$
\frac{\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{3\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }=\frac{1}{3}
$$
